name: Introduction to homelabbing featuring Ben Heater
description:
🔔 Join us on a webinar featuring Ben Heater from Dark Wolf Solutions, a systems and security engineer and penetration tester, in exploring the world of home labs.

 

🤔 What are Home Labs:

    A home lab is a personal tech playground where you can experiment, learn, and build. The practice includes setting up servers, playing with networks, trying out cybersecurity tools - the possibilities are endless. A practical use-case is setting up a "self-hosted" server to keep your files and media to avoid paying a pricey subscription. In Ben Heater's own words, "home labs are one of the single greatest ways to develop core skill sets in IT."

 

🤵 About our speaker, Ben Heater:

    Ben Heater works for Dark Wolf Solutions as a Senior Associate Penetration Tester. In the past, he's worked as a cyber network analysis tech, security specialist, IT systems engineer/admin, and more. For more information about his professional experience, make sure to check his LinkedIn. Outside of work, Ben also keeps a blog where he shares information about home labs, ethical hacking, and other IT/Cybersecurity topics, make sure to check it out here.

 

📜 About the webinar:

    In this webinar, Ben Heater will introduce you to home labs, why they're important, and walk you through the steps to building your own home lab. He will share the pros and cons of a home lab, the typical progression of a home lab setup, common designs, equipment, where and how to start. By the end of the event, you will be equipped with the knowledge of what can be accomplished through homelabbing, and how to dive into this amazing practice. If you're interested in tech or cybersecurity, you can't miss this webinar!

name: Version Control with Git & Collaboration on GitHub Workshop
description:
🔔 Join us for a hands-on workshop on mastering Git and GitHub!

 

👨‍💻 About the workshop:

In this session, participants will learn how to track and manage code changes using Git, collaborate effectively with others through GitHub, and follow best practices for version control. Through live demonstrations, you’ll see how to create repositories, commit changes, branch and merge code, and contribute to projects using pull requests. By the end of the workshop, you’ll have the practical skills to confidently manage projects and collaborate in a team environment.

 

❓What is Git/Github?

Git is a “version control system” that lets you track and manage changes to your code over time, like a “save history” for your projects. It helps you experiment, fix mistakes, and keep everything organized. It is an essential tool for anyone working with code.

GitHub is an online platform that works with Git, making it easy to share code, collaborate with others, and contribute to open-source projects. Together, they’re essential tools for any developer working in a team or managing personal projects. Github is used by millions of developers, and you will be expected to know it at some point in your software development journey.

More details in the workshop, we hope to see you there!

name: Understanding Databases: SQL vs NoSQL (PostgreSQL & MongoDB) Workshop
description:
🔔 Join us for an interactive workshop on mastering databases with PostgreSQL and MongoDB!

 

👨‍💻 About the workshop:

In this session, participants will explore the fundamental concepts that power modern data management. You’ll dive into the key differences between relational and non-relational databases, focusing on two leading technologies: PostgreSQL and MongoDB. Through guided explanations and live demonstrations, you’ll see how data is structured, stored, and queried in each system. By the end, you’ll have a solid foundation in both SQL and NoSQL paradigms and a better understanding of how databases drive real-world software systems.

 

🧠 What you’ll learn:

- The role and purpose of databases
- Differences between SQL and NoSQL systems
- Overview of relational databases (PostgreSQL) and non-relational databases (MongoDB)
- Practical examples with Redis and other database technologies
- Live PostgreSQL demo: creating tables, inserting data, and running queries

 

🤵 About our speaker:

This workshop will be led by Gabriel Morales, a CSA board member and experienced developer passionate about backend systems and data-driven applications. This session marks the third part of our ongoing workshop series, following previous events on frontend and backend development.

name: Podman & Containerization Workshop
description:
A workshop about Podman by the Computer Science Association, featuring Evan Carroll. Podman (pod manager) is an open source tool for managing containers (similar to Docker) available on Windows, Linux, and MacOS systems.

What are containers?
Containers are a way to package an application together with everything it needs to run (libraries, tools, settings) so it behaves the same on any computer. Instead of installing software directly on your system, you can do it inside a container which is isolated, making it easy to start or remove. Podman is a tool, similar to Docker, which lets you download, start, stop, and delete these containerized applications.

Why use Podman and similar tools?
Using tools like Podman helps avoid “it works on my machine” problems by ensuring software runs the same everywhere, while also reducing the risk of breaking your system.

🤵 About our speaker, Evan Carroll:
Evan Carroll is a seasoned Software Engineer and a prominent figure in the Houston technology scene. Throughout his career, he has navigated nearly every layer of the stack, serving as a systems administrator, database specialist, and senior software engineer. Currently, he leverages his deep expertise in Rust and Linux systems to build high-performance software. For more information about his professional journey, make sure to check his [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/evancarroll/).

Outside of his professional roles, Evan is a passionate advocate for the open-source movement. He is a founding member of the Houston Open Source Society (HOSS) and has contributed to massive global projects including Node.js, OpenStreetMap, and Wikidata. He is a frequent face at local tech meetups and hackathons, where he enjoys sharing his knowledge on everything from PostgreSQL optimization to modern containerization with Podman.

Gabriel Morales is a software engineer and educator passionate about modern development workflows and AI-assisted tooling. He brings hands-on experience building production back-end systems and a talent for making cutting-edge tools accessible to students.


🗂️ What you'll cover:

  • Setting up Cursor and Claude Code accounts
  • Defining your tech stack and configuring project context & rules in Cursor for FastAPI
  • Initial project setup and automation methodologies in Cursor
  • Running a Python development environment inside a Docker container
  • Database migrations and ORM model creation with Alembic and SQLAlchemy
  • Building services and API endpoints in FastAPI with Docker
  • Writing unit tests with pytest and mocking


👥 Who should attend?

  • Students curious about AI-assisted development
  • Developers who want to ship back-end projects faster
  • Anyone interested in tools like Cursor, Claude Code, FastAPI, or Docker

description:

name: Git & GitHub 101: Version Control from the Command Line
description:
💡 About the workshop:

Whether you're pushing your first commit or trying to finally wrap your head around branching, this workshop has you covered. Join us for a hands-on deep dive into Git and GitHub, two tools that are practically non-negotiable in modern software development. Through live command-line demos, you'll build real, practical fluency with version control from the ground up.

👤 About the speaker: Nelson Aviles

Nelson is a second-year Computer Science student and officer of the Computer Science Association. Having experienced the frustration of not knowing how to use Git in a team setting, he's here to teach you the basics so you don't go through the same struggles.

🗂️ What you'll cover:

  • Setting up and initializing a Git repository
  • Staging, committing, and tracking changes from the command line
  • Working with branches and merging strategies
  • Resolving merge conflicts
  • Collaborating on GitHub via pull requests and code review workflows

👥 Who should attend?

  • Students who are new to version control and want to learn it right from the start
  • Developers who've used Git casually but want a more confident, structured understanding
  • Anyone preparing for internships, projects, or open-source contributions

name: HackHCC: CodeRunners
description:
⚡ HackHCC: CodeRunners ⚡ 
A Cyberpunk-themed Hackathon

Step into the neon-lit future and put your skills to the test at HackHCC: CodeRunners, Houston Community College’s first large, official hackathon. Inspired by Cyberpunk 2077, this event brings together creativity, technology, and collaboration for an unforgettable 24+ hour build experience.

💡 What is a hackathon?
A hackathon is an event where participants form teams and build a project (an app, game, website, or tool) within a limited time. You’ll learn by doing, collaborate with others, and turn ideas into something real, all in a supportive and fast-paced environment.

🌱 Why beginners should attend:
You do not need to be an expert to participate. Hackathons are one of the best ways to learn new skills, meet other students, and gain real experience outside the classroom. Whether you’re brand new to coding or already building projects, there’s a place for you here. Mentors, workshops, and team collaboration will help guide you every step of the way.

🚀 What to expect:

  • A cyberpunk-themed atmosphere

  • Team-based project building

  • Networking opportunities with sponsors

  • Workshops and mentor support

  • Prizes, swag, and surprises

  • Overnight hacking experience

  • 200–300 students from across HCC and beyond

🤝 Powered by collaboration:
HackHCC: CodeRunners is organized in partnership with Major League Hacking (MLH). Sponsors will be announced soon.

📍 Venue:
West Houston Institute – Auditorium
(Overnight stay permitted)

📅 Date:
Friday, May 22 – Saturday, May 23 (Week after final exams)
⏱️ Event times are subject to change
